While renewable energy plays a central role in climate mitigation, it cannot alone eliminate fossil fuel dependence due to electrification limits, storage challenges, and sectoral constraints. Bioeconomy strategies complement renewables by leveraging biological systems to capture, substitute, and remove atmospheric CO₂. These strategies are organized into three pathways: photosynthesis, thermochemical conversion, and microbial processes.
